jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization.

The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management

Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness.
Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options.
Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks.

AI Solution Development & Implementation

Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities.
Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working.
Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement.
Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured.
Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk.

AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption

Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption.
Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks.
Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements.
Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed.
Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required.

Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management

Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users.
Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI.
Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support.
Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement.
Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption

Vendor, Technology & Partner Management

Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership.
Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization.
Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation.
Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value.

Qualifications, Skills, And Educational Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption.
Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI.
Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.
Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office)
Fast paced office environment
Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees across multiple facilities in the Greater Toronto Area. We are adding a Director of Information Technology to our leadership team — a senior role with full ownership of the IT function and a direct hand in how this business operates and grows.

The scope is deliberately broad. Liteline is investing in artificial intelligence, automation, data infrastructure and connected business systems across the organization, and the Director of Information Technology will lead that work from the front.

This is an operating role as much as a technical one. The person in this position will work closely with leadership and with departments across the business, including Operations, Customer Service, Sales, Finance, Product Development, Manufacturing, Warehousing and Distribution.

IT Strategy and Leadership

Own and develop Liteline's IT strategy and long-term technology roadmap.
Partner directly with senior leadership to set technology priorities and identify risks and investment opportunities.
Evaluate emerging technologies and determine where they create real operational or commercial value.
Maintain and evolve the standards, policies and governance practices a growing organization requires.
Lead technology planning across multiple facilities and business functions.
Own IT budgets, capital planning, licensing, vendor spend and major technology investments.
Lead the internal IT team and the external partners who support IT and set the service standards the business is held to.

AI, Automation and Digital Transformation

Lead Liteline's adoption of artificial intelligence, automation and next-generation business technologies.
Find the highest-value applications for automation across the business and build the case for them.
Develop AI and automation solutions that lift productivity, sharpen decision-making and strengthen the customer experience.
Build the infrastructure and governance required to scale AI responsibly across the organization.
Work directly with business leaders to move successful initiatives from experimentation into production.
Embed data and automation into everyday business operations.

Business Systems and Data

Own the architecture and ongoing development of Liteline's core business systems.
Oversee ERP, databases, reporting systems, integrations and other enterprise applications.
Own the platforms supporting our customer-facing teams, including order management, pricing and product information.
Own system integration and the flow of information between departments and facilities.
Lead Liteline's data strategy, covering structure, accessibility, security, integration, reporting and business intelligence.
Partner with functions across the business on system capability, visibility and usability.
Keep technology platforms scalable and aligned to where the business is heading.

Cybersecurity, Infrastructure and Business Continuity

Own Liteline's cybersecurity strategy, policies, controls and risk-management framework.
Maintain a strong security posture across endpoints, servers, networks, cloud services, applications and user access.
Oversee infrastructure including servers, networking, storage, virtualization, cloud environments and telecommunications.
Maintain tested backup, disaster-recovery and business-continuity capability.
Maintain the monitoring, patching and access-control practices that keep the environment defensible.
Manage external technology and cybersecurity partners.
Keep infrastructure stable, secure, scalable and resilient.

Technology Operations

Maintain high availability and reliability across critical systems.
Own the service standards, escalation paths and accountability for technology issues.
Deliver a technology experience that makes it easy for more than 160 employees to do their best work.
Manage relationships with key technology vendors, service providers and consultants.
Keep Liteline's platforms and commercial arrangements current, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.
Deliver projects on scope, on schedule and with the documentation to support them.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for an experienced technology leader who operates comfortably at both the strategic and the technical level.

The successful candidate will understand enterprise infrastructure, business applications, cybersecurity, data and emerging technologies, and will also understand that technology exists to serve the business. You should be able to step onto the floor, understand how the work is genuinely performed, and design practical solutions that people adopt and keep using.

Strong candidates will bring:
Significant experience leading information technology in a complex business environment.
Strong knowledge of IT infrastructure, networking, servers, cloud technologies and enterprise systems.
Experience with cybersecurity strategy, governance, risk management and business continuity.
A strong grasp of databases, systems integration, data architecture and business intelligence.
Experience with ERP and other enterprise business applications.
Practical understanding of artificial intelligence, automation and modern development technologies.
A record of leading major technology projects from strategy through implementation.
Strong vendor-management and commercial-negotiation skills.
The ability to communicate effectively with senior executives as well as operational and technical stakeholders.
Sound business judgment and the ability to prioritize technology initiatives by business impact.

LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week, with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a rare chance to take full ownership of technology at an established Canadian manufacturer with the scale to matter and the appetite to move quickly.

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. The Director of Information Technology will help define what this company's technology environment becomes over the next several years, and will have the mandate, the budget and the executive support to build it.

For the right leader, this is the opportunity to put their signature on how a growing Canadian manufacturer runs.

WHAT WE OFFER

Liteline offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision and life insurance following three months of service, and a group RRSP with partial company match.

TO APPLY

Qualified candidates are invited to apply directly through this posting.

Liteline Corporation is an equal opportunity employer that values the unique skills and experiences of every candidate. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and hiring process. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources with the position title in the subject line.

Children’s Treatment Network (CTN) supports over 42,000 kids and youth with disabilities and other developmental needs. We provide intake, service navigation and coordinated service planning, assessment and diagnostic services, specialized clinics and rehabilitation services, including physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech language therapy.

Funded by the Ministry of Children, Community and Social Services, CTN is an Ontario provincial government funded not-for profit organization, that offers services through contracted partners in the education, health and community sectors. Through its innovative network model, CTN’s commitment to providing family-centered care is anchored by an electronic client record that is shared across its partner organizations and provides the foundation for integrated plans of care and services.

Our goal is a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We welcome all qualified applicants to apply including individuals with disabilities, those who identify as Black, Indigenous or persons of colour, members of the LGBTQ2S+ communities and others. We are proud to be in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA), 2005 and the Integrated Accessibility Standards Regulation. We are happy to honour accommodations at any part of the recruitment process and invite you to let us know how we can help.

What We Offer:

Competitive compensation and employee benefits package including participation in the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP) and vacation/leave entitlement
An opportunity to contribute to the work of a not-for-profit organization that provides services to kids and youth with disabilities and developmental needs and their families
The opportunity to work with us to achieve CTN’s strategic goals of putting people at the centre of what we do, striving for excellence, fostering a culture of accountability and stewardship to support community needs, and transformation through equitable data-driven service innovation

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Jim Peplinski Capital

At most companies, finance supports the business. At Jim Peplinski Capital (JPC), finance is our business.

For over 35 years, Jim Peplinski Capital has financed and managed the vehicles and equipment Canadian businesses run on. We combine capital, fleet expertise and technology to help our clients get the most from the assets that keep them moving. Now we're building the next generation of fleet management, with ambitious growth plans and the balance sheet to pursue them.

We're looking for a steady, strategic, and commercially minded CFO to partner with the President and Executive Team on the decisions and execution that shape our future.

About The Role

Reporting directly to the President, you'll lead JPC's Finance, Credit and Risk function and serve as a trusted partner to the Executive Team. Two leaders report to you, a Finance Manager and a Credit Manager, along with their teams.

This is not a back-office finance role. As a lender and fleet manager, how we fund, price and manage risk is how we compete, and you'll own it. That covers capital and liquidity, funding and banking relationships, pricing and return on capital, portfolio risk and credit discipline, financial reporting and planning, and accounting, controls and compliance.

You'll shape how JPC funds its growth, manages risk, allocates capital, and you'll build the people and systems we need to scale. It's hands-on leadership: you set the direction, and you’ll roll up your sleeves when the work calls for it.

What You’ll Do

Team Leadership. Build, mentor and develop high-performing Finance and Credit teams with a culture of sound judgment, ownership, accountability and practical problem solving.
Capital, Funding and Liquidity. Ensure JPC has the capital, liquidity and funding structure to support growth. You'll manage banking relationships, funding facilities, interest rate exposure, covenant compliance and lender reporting, and build capacity ahead of where the business is going.
Residuals and Portfolio Risk. You'll own concentration limits, provisioning and credit performance across the portfolio. Collaborating with our VP, Asset Management, you'll set and monitor residual assumptions.
Credit and Adjudication. Keep credit discipline strong while finding practical ways to say yes to good business. You'll be the second set of eyes for the Credit Manager on the decisions that need it.
Financial Reporting and Planning. Deliver accurate, timely reporting to the President, Board and lenders. You'll lead budgeting, forecasting and planning, and provide the Executive Team the insights to make better decisions faster.
Accounting, Compliance and Controls. Own accounting, lease accounting, tax, audit, treasury and financial controls, plus our regulatory program, including FINTRAC and AML.
Client engagement. Work directly with clients on the decisions that matter most, from structuring deals to managing delinquencies and payment workouts, balancing a strong relationship with protecting the portfolio.
Commercial Judgment. Bring financial rigor to decisions on new products, services and partner programs. You'll lead negotiation of key commercial agreements and embed financial and risk thinking across JPC.
Systems & Technology: Own the finance and credit systems that support our growth, driving automation and building a scalable foundation for reporting, adjudication and accounting.

What We’re Looking For

You have 12+ years of progressive finance experience, including senior leadership. Experience in fleet management, automotive and/or equipment finance or specialty lending is a strong asset. Bank or boutique, we care about the depth of your experience, not the logo. A CPA is preferred but not required for candidates with deep experience as a CFO or senior finance leader in a lending business.

You Also

Have built teams, developed strong leaders, and held them to a high standard.
Understand banking, lending, capital structure and liquidity management.
Have excellent financial, accounting and commercial credit judgment.
Are an expert in assessing financial performance, cash flow, leverage and creditworthiness.
Turn financial information into clear recommendations and decisions.
Can protect the balance sheet without losing sight of the customer and commercial opportunities.
Take ownership, challenge assumptions and make decisions.

Why You’ll Love It At JPC

A real partnership. You'll work directly with the President, Executive Team and Board. We're privately held, so decisions get made quickly, and you'll be part of making them.
Autonomy to build. You'll have the autonomy to build our Finance, Credit and Risk function, influence strategy and create processes that scale.
A chance to shape the industry. You'll help define how commercial fleets are financed and optimized.
A team that plays to win. You'll join a talented, fast-moving group that values ownership, high standards and trust.
Strong rewards. Competitive compensation, a performance bonus, and comprehensive benefits from day one.

Define and drive the platform roadmap aligned with product and business goals.

Lead the development of the data pipeline, integrating with Blackpoint’s endpoint agent and vendor data, including storage, tiered access, and query capabilities.

Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.

Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.

Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

Internal Controls

Audit Functions
Capital Planning

Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.

Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

new_jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
new_jobs.description:
Liteline Corporation is a privately held Canadian lighting manufacturer with more than 160 employees across multiple facilities in the Greater Toronto Area. We are adding a Director of Information Technology to our leadership team — a senior role with full ownership of the IT function and a direct hand in how this business operates and grows.

The scope is deliberately broad. Liteline is investing in artificial intelligence, automation, data infrastructure and connected business systems across the organization, and the Director of Information Technology will lead that work from the front.

This is an operating role as much as a technical one. The person in this position will work closely with leadership and with departments across the business, including Operations, Customer Service, Sales, Finance, Product Development, Manufacturing, Warehousing and Distribution.

IT Strategy and Leadership

Own and develop Liteline's IT strategy and long-term technology roadmap.
Partner directly with senior leadership to set technology priorities and identify risks and investment opportunities.
Evaluate emerging technologies and determine where they create real operational or commercial value.
Maintain and evolve the standards, policies and governance practices a growing organization requires.
Lead technology planning across multiple facilities and business functions.
Own IT budgets, capital planning, licensing, vendor spend and major technology investments.
Lead the internal IT team and the external partners who support IT and set the service standards the business is held to.

AI, Automation and Digital Transformation

Lead Liteline's adoption of artificial intelligence, automation and next-generation business technologies.
Find the highest-value applications for automation across the business and build the case for them.
Develop AI and automation solutions that lift productivity, sharpen decision-making and strengthen the customer experience.
Build the infrastructure and governance required to scale AI responsibly across the organization.
Work directly with business leaders to move successful initiatives from experimentation into production.
Embed data and automation into everyday business operations.

Business Systems and Data

Own the architecture and ongoing development of Liteline's core business systems.
Oversee ERP, databases, reporting systems, integrations and other enterprise applications.
Own the platforms supporting our customer-facing teams, including order management, pricing and product information.
Own system integration and the flow of information between departments and facilities.
Lead Liteline's data strategy, covering structure, accessibility, security, integration, reporting and business intelligence.
Partner with functions across the business on system capability, visibility and usability.
Keep technology platforms scalable and aligned to where the business is heading.

Cybersecurity, Infrastructure and Business Continuity

Own Liteline's cybersecurity strategy, policies, controls and risk-management framework.
Maintain a strong security posture across endpoints, servers, networks, cloud services, applications and user access.
Oversee infrastructure including servers, networking, storage, virtualization, cloud environments and telecommunications.
Maintain tested backup, disaster-recovery and business-continuity capability.
Maintain the monitoring, patching and access-control practices that keep the environment defensible.
Manage external technology and cybersecurity partners.
Keep infrastructure stable, secure, scalable and resilient.

Technology Operations

Maintain high availability and reliability across critical systems.
Own the service standards, escalation paths and accountability for technology issues.
Deliver a technology experience that makes it easy for more than 160 employees to do their best work.
Manage relationships with key technology vendors, service providers and consultants.
Keep Liteline's platforms and commercial arrangements current, and bring forward stronger options as the market moves.
Deliver projects on scope, on schedule and with the documentation to support them.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for an experienced technology leader who operates comfortably at both the strategic and the technical level.

The successful candidate will understand enterprise infrastructure, business applications, cybersecurity, data and emerging technologies, and will also understand that technology exists to serve the business. You should be able to step onto the floor, understand how the work is genuinely performed, and design practical solutions that people adopt and keep using.

Strong candidates will bring:
Significant experience leading information technology in a complex business environment.
Strong knowledge of IT infrastructure, networking, servers, cloud technologies and enterprise systems.
Experience with cybersecurity strategy, governance, risk management and business continuity.
A strong grasp of databases, systems integration, data architecture and business intelligence.
Experience with ERP and other enterprise business applications.
Practical understanding of artificial intelligence, automation and modern development technologies.
A record of leading major technology projects from strategy through implementation.
Strong vendor-management and commercial-negotiation skills.
The ability to communicate effectively with senior executives as well as operational and technical stakeholders.
Sound business judgment and the ability to prioritize technology initiatives by business impact.

LOCATION AND WORKING ARRANGEMENT

This position is based at Liteline's Richmond Hill head office and is on-site five days per week, with regular presence at our distribution facilities.

The successful candidate should expect to be highly engaged with the business and to spend real time understanding how departments and facilities actually operate.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a rare chance to take full ownership of technology at an established Canadian manufacturer with the scale to matter and the appetite to move quickly.

Liteline is privately held, decisions are made without layers of approval, and good ideas get backed. The Director of Information Technology will help define what this company's technology environment becomes over the next several years, and will have the mandate, the budget and the executive support to build it.

For the right leader, this is the opportunity to put their signature on how a growing Canadian manufacturer runs.

WHAT WE OFFER

Liteline offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision and life insurance following three months of service, and a group RRSP with partial company match.

TO APPLY

Qualified candidates are invited to apply directly through this posting.

Liteline Corporation is an equal opportunity employer that values the unique skills and experiences of every candidate. We are committed to accommodating people with disabilities throughout the recruitment and hiring process. To request accommodation, please contact Human Resources with the position title in the subject line.

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
new_jobs.description:
About Jim Peplinski Capital

At most companies, finance supports the business. At Jim Peplinski Capital (JPC), finance is our business.

For over 35 years, Jim Peplinski Capital has financed and managed the vehicles and equipment Canadian businesses run on. We combine capital, fleet expertise and technology to help our clients get the most from the assets that keep them moving. Now we're building the next generation of fleet management, with ambitious growth plans and the balance sheet to pursue them.

We're looking for a steady, strategic, and commercially minded CFO to partner with the President and Executive Team on the decisions and execution that shape our future.

About The Role

Reporting directly to the President, you'll lead JPC's Finance, Credit and Risk function and serve as a trusted partner to the Executive Team. Two leaders report to you, a Finance Manager and a Credit Manager, along with their teams.

This is not a back-office finance role. As a lender and fleet manager, how we fund, price and manage risk is how we compete, and you'll own it. That covers capital and liquidity, funding and banking relationships, pricing and return on capital, portfolio risk and credit discipline, financial reporting and planning, and accounting, controls and compliance.

You'll shape how JPC funds its growth, manages risk, allocates capital, and you'll build the people and systems we need to scale. It's hands-on leadership: you set the direction, and you’ll roll up your sleeves when the work calls for it.

What You’ll Do

Team Leadership. Build, mentor and develop high-performing Finance and Credit teams with a culture of sound judgment, ownership, accountability and practical problem solving.
Capital, Funding and Liquidity. Ensure JPC has the capital, liquidity and funding structure to support growth. You'll manage banking relationships, funding facilities, interest rate exposure, covenant compliance and lender reporting, and build capacity ahead of where the business is going.
Residuals and Portfolio Risk. You'll own concentration limits, provisioning and credit performance across the portfolio. Collaborating with our VP, Asset Management, you'll set and monitor residual assumptions.
Credit and Adjudication. Keep credit discipline strong while finding practical ways to say yes to good business. You'll be the second set of eyes for the Credit Manager on the decisions that need it.
Financial Reporting and Planning. Deliver accurate, timely reporting to the President, Board and lenders. You'll lead budgeting, forecasting and planning, and provide the Executive Team the insights to make better decisions faster.
Accounting, Compliance and Controls. Own accounting, lease accounting, tax, audit, treasury and financial controls, plus our regulatory program, including FINTRAC and AML.
Client engagement. Work directly with clients on the decisions that matter most, from structuring deals to managing delinquencies and payment workouts, balancing a strong relationship with protecting the portfolio.
Commercial Judgment. Bring financial rigor to decisions on new products, services and partner programs. You'll lead negotiation of key commercial agreements and embed financial and risk thinking across JPC.
Systems & Technology: Own the finance and credit systems that support our growth, driving automation and building a scalable foundation for reporting, adjudication and accounting.

What We’re Looking For

You have 12+ years of progressive finance experience, including senior leadership. Experience in fleet management, automotive and/or equipment finance or specialty lending is a strong asset. Bank or boutique, we care about the depth of your experience, not the logo. A CPA is preferred but not required for candidates with deep experience as a CFO or senior finance leader in a lending business.

You Also

Have built teams, developed strong leaders, and held them to a high standard.
Understand banking, lending, capital structure and liquidity management.
Have excellent financial, accounting and commercial credit judgment.
Are an expert in assessing financial performance, cash flow, leverage and creditworthiness.
Turn financial information into clear recommendations and decisions.
Can protect the balance sheet without losing sight of the customer and commercial opportunities.
Take ownership, challenge assumptions and make decisions.

Why You’ll Love It At JPC

A real partnership. You'll work directly with the President, Executive Team and Board. We're privately held, so decisions get made quickly, and you'll be part of making them.
Autonomy to build. You'll have the autonomy to build our Finance, Credit and Risk function, influence strategy and create processes that scale.
A chance to shape the industry. You'll help define how commercial fleets are financed and optimized.
A team that plays to win. You'll join a talented, fast-moving group that values ownership, high standards and trust.
Strong rewards. Competitive compensation, a performance bonus, and comprehensive benefits from day one.

new_jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

________________________________________

Procurement Governance

Establish financial oversight and governance for procurement activities.
Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

________________________________________

Indigenous Relations & Partnership Development

Build and maintain respectful relationships with Tsuut'ina Nation leadership and stakeholders.
Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

________________________________________

Stakeholder Management

The CFO Will Maintain Productive Relationships With

Internal Stakeholders

Board of Directors
Executive Leadership Team
Department Leaders
Team Members

External Stakeholders

Tsuut'ina Nation Leadership
Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC)
Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC)
Auditors
Financial Institutions
Legal Counsel
Development Partners
Government Agencies
Industry Associations
Consultants and Contractors

________________________________________

Risk Management & Governance

Lead enterprise risk management activities.
Ensure effective internal controls and compliance programs.
Support Board governance and Finance & Audit Committee activities.
Oversee annual external audits.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and accounting standards.
Develop financial risk mitigation strategies.

________________________________________

BOARD FINANCE & AUDIT COMMITTEE SUPPORT

The CFO serves as management's primary liaison to the Finance and Audit Committee and is responsible for:

Preparing committee materials and recommendations.
Presenting financial results and forecasts.
Supporting audit processes.
Monitoring risk management activities.
Reporting on compliance and internal controls.
Supporting governance best practices.

Priority will be given to Tsuut'ina Nation members.
